title: fix(components,core): a protocol placeholder never takes a key a pending lazy stub owns (objectui#11680)
body:
Fixes #11680

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

The console declares `view:calendar` and `view:timeline` as `registerLazy` stubs in `apps/console/src/register-plugins.ts` (`registerLazy('calendar', …, { namespace: 'view' })`, the same for `timeline`), then calls `registerPlaceholders()` from `main.tsx`. `registerPlaceholder` guarded with `ComponentRegistry.get(type)`, which answers for LOADED registrations only. So both keys read as free while their stubs were pending. The placeholder registered as `protocol-placeholder:view:calendar` and took the bare key `view:calendar`, which is the stub's own full key. The registry's eager door then cleared the stub under that key, as it does for any key a registration takes. Until some other node loaded the calendar or timeline chunk, an authored `view:calendar` / `view:timeline` drew the dashed "Component Placeholder" box, and every boot logged the race warning once per key.

The warning read `view:view:calendar` because `lazyStubFullType` re-derived a stub's claim as "the entry's namespace, prefixed onto the key it was looked up under". `registerLazy` stores one entry under two keys, its full key and its bare key, so a lookup that landed on the full key doubled the namespace.

## The change

- **`@object-ui/components`, `registerPlaceholder`:** returns early when `ComponentRegistry.hasLazy(type)` is true, before the existing loaded-registration check. `hasLazy` is already public, so the registry gains no API. The line `if (!ComponentRegistry.get(type))` is kept verbatim because `check:registry-bare-names` re-reads that exact text (`GUARDED_INDIRECT_SITES` in `scripts/check-registry-bare-name-collisions.mjs`), so that script needs no edit.
- **`@object-ui/core`, `Registry`:** a lazy entry records its `fullType` on the line in `registerLazy` that computes the key it is stored under. The three readers now read `entry.fullType`: the eager door's cross-table warning, the lazy door's prior-stub warning, and the bare-stub ownership test in `unregister`. `lazyStubFullType` is removed: re-deriving the claim from the lookup key was the defect, and there is nothing left for it to compute.

Published declarations are byte-identical: `packages/core/dist/registry/Registry.d.ts` built at the base (`9ca3cac`, Registry.ts swapped in under a trap and restored, blob == HEAD) and at head compare equal (`cmp` exit 0, sha256 prefix `893dd7070a53757b` both). `LazyEntry` is not exported and `lazyEntries` is `private`. `registerPlaceholder` is not exported, so `packages/components/dist/renderers/placeholders.d.ts` carries no docblock this diff touched. The claim's `Clause-②: no` holds.

## Premise checks (the order's mechanism assumptions, measured at `9ca3cac`)

1. **Path:** `packages/components/src/registry/Registry.ts` does not exist. The registry is `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts`. Confirmed.
2. **`get()` ignores pending stubs:** confirmed on a fresh `Registry` with only `registerLazy('calendar', …, { namespace: 'view' })`: `get('view:calendar')` undefined, `has('view:calendar')` false, `hasLazy('view:calendar')` true, `getKnownTypes()` includes it.
3. **Who passes the already-namespaced type:** the placeholder, `register('view:calendar', PlaceholderRenderer, { namespace: 'protocol-placeholder' })`. Its bare key is the stub's full key. The stub side is not doubled. The same doubling sat in `registerLazy`'s prior-stub claim and in `unregister`'s ownership test, and both are pinned below.
4. **Where the producer is:** `PALETTE_PLACEHOLDER_BLOCKS`, the eager side effect, is not the producer for these keys. It holds `nav:menu`, `nav:breadcrumb`, `global:search` and `ai:suggestion` only. The `view:*` placeholders come from `registerPlaceholders()`. So the pin replays `registerPlaceholders()`.
5. **Census:** `registerPlaceholders()` has one non-test caller, `apps/console/src/main.tsx`. `registerPlaceholder` has two call sites, both in `placeholders.tsx`: the `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` loop and the palette side effect. Lazy registrations whose full type is `view:*`: two, `timeline` and `calendar`, both in `register-plugins.ts`. Re-derive with `git grep -nE -A2 'registerLazy\(' -- 'apps/*/src/**' 'packages/*/src/**' | grep "namespace: 'view'"`. No host depends on the placeholder winning a stubbed key: nothing calls `registerPlaceholders()` anywhere else, and no test asserts a `protocol-placeholder:view:*` key.

## One-time full-load measurement (a scratch probe, deleted before commit, not a live pin)

The probe imported the console's real `register-plugins.ts`, called the real `registerPlaceholders()`, then `loadLazy` on both keys (the real `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` / `plugin-timeline` chunks), counting `bare-name fallback` warnings:

| | import phase | placeholder phase | after placeholders | after the real chunks load |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `9ca3cac` | 0 | 2 (`view:calendar`, `view:timeline`, both naming `view:view:…`) | `view:calendar` resolves to `protocol-placeholder:view:calendar`; `hasLazy` false | not taken |
| fix (Registry.ts and placeholders.tsx bytes as at head) | 0 | 0 | both keys unresolved, `hasLazy` true | `view:calendar` resolves to "Calendar View", `view:timeline` to "Timeline View"; 0 warnings |

## Pins

- `apps/console/src/__tests__/full-load-placeholder-race-11680.test.ts` (console project; patch round 1): the live full-load pin. It replays the boot `main.tsx` performs over the console's REAL stub list, `../register-plugins`, and then calls the real `registerPlaceholders()`. It asserts that the whole load emits no bare-name race warning. The capture is installed in `vi.hoisted`, ahead of the imports, because the stubs register while `register-plugins` is imported. **Positive control**, in the same file: every key a stub held before the placeholders registered is still held after them (`hasLazy`), and that set includes `view:calendar` and `view:timeline`, so the silence covers the two keys the card measured. Because it reads the real list, the next console stub that a placeholder races turns this pin red, with no new card. No console source is edited.
- `packages/components/src/__tests__/placeholder-lazy-stub-ownership-11680.test.tsx` (`dom` project, isolated): stubs declared with the console's arguments, each chunk gated so it lands on command and registers the way the plugin does. Uses the real `registerPlaceholders()` and the real `SchemaRenderer`. **Console boot order**, for `view:calendar` and `view:timeline`: no race warning when the placeholders register or when the chunk lands. Before the load, `get()` is not `PlaceholderRenderer` and `hasLazy()` is true, and an authored node never shows "Component Placeholder" and renders the plugin once the chunk lands. After the load, `get()` is the plugin's renderer. **Controls:** chunk-loaded-first order (unchanged behaviour), and a protocol key nothing owns (`view:kanban`) still gets the placeholder. The two node types are declared through `CustomNodeRegistry`, the way an application declares a type it registers, rather than cast.
- `packages/core/src/registry/__tests__/Registry.test.ts`, block `a stub found under its FULL key names that full type once (objectui#11680)`: the eager door names the stub `view:calendar`, with no `view:view:`. The eager door still reports a registration whose own full type is the doubled spelling: before, the doubled claim equalled it, so the guard said nothing. The lazy door names the prior stub `view:calendar`. `unregister('view:calendar', 'view')` leaves the console's stub: before, it deleted it.
- `packages/plugin-report/src/__tests__/ReportRenderer.test.tsx` (patch round 1, the CI red at `409496f`): the suite replaces `ComponentRegistry` with a hand-built partial stub, `{ get, register }`. The palette placeholder side effect, which `@object-ui/components` runs at module load, now calls `hasLazy()` first, so the suite failed at import with `TypeError: ComponentRegistry.hasLazy is not a function` (`Test (shard 6/8)`). The stub gains `hasLazy`, a `vi.fn` that answers `false`, because no stub is pending in that suite. Its assertions are unchanged, and the registrar does not tolerate a missing method. It is the only `vi.mock('@object-ui/core')` in the tree that hand-builds `ComponentRegistry`: the other two spread the real module. Red reproduced locally (the placeholder and suite bytes at `bdcd1a9` equal those at `409496f`): `TypeError: ComponentRegistry.hasLazy is not a function`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)`. Green after: `Tests 3 passed (3)`.

## Ablation and reverse verification (one-shot, all from committed state)

- **Guard reverted, against the components pin** (anchor `if (ComponentRegistry.hasLazy(type)) return;` deleted through `ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `202f3062ae59` → `e8a66e1276cb`). Predicted: both console-boot rows red, the three controls green. Observed at `409496f`: `Tests 2 failed | 3 passed (5)`, both failing on `registering the placeholders raced the stub: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []`. Restore proven: blob == HEAD (`202f3062ae59`), `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Guard reverted, against the console full-load pin** (same anchor, same tool). Predicted: red on the race assertion, naming both keys. Observed at `bdcd1a9`: `Tests 1 failed (1)` on `a registration took a bare key another declaration holds: expected [ …(2) ] to deeply equal []`, the two captured warnings being the `view:calendar` and `view:timeline` races, each now naming the stub's claim once (`claims for "view:calendar"`). Restore proven: blob == HEAD (`202f3062ae59`), `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Doubling fix reverted** (`Registry.ts` replaced by its `9ca3cac` blob `69457e1f5bb2` under an EXIT/INT/TERM trap with an absolute path). Predicted: the four new Registry pins red, the rest green. Observed at `18b8a39`: `Tests 4 failed | 55 passed (59)`: claimant `'view:view:calendar'` twice, `expected [] to have a length of 1` for the silent guard, and `unregister` deleting the stub. Restore proven: blob == HEAD (`c7d525e29bc9`), `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Resolution path: vitest aliases `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/components` and `@object-ui/react` to `src`, so no leg needed a rebuild of `dist`.

## Gates

Declared to CI, not run locally: the full `pnpm test` shards, repo-wide `pnpm lint`, and the remaining workflows. CI at `409496f` was red on `Test (shard 6/8)` and the aggregate `Test` only, which is the `ReportRenderer` suite above.

Changeset: `.changeset/11680-placeholder-lazy-stub-guard.md`, `patch` for `@object-ui/components` and `@object-ui/core`.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

1. **Placeholder-first order.** The guard is checked when the placeholder registers, so a stub declared after a placeholder would still find the key taken until its chunk loads. Producers on this tree: the palette side effect runs at `@object-ui/components` import, before any host stub, but none of its four keys is stubbed anywhere. `registerPlaceholders()`'s one caller runs after the console's stubs. No producer, so noted only. Carrier: none.
2. **The eager door clears a stub stored under its FULL key.** When a registration's bare key equals another stub's full type, the delete in `register`'s fallback branch removes that stub's canonical entry, not a bare one. That is how the placeholder erased `view:calendar`'s stub. With the placeholder fixed, no registration here has a colon-shaped bare key that equals another stub's full type, so the shape is dormant. Carrier: none.
3. **`getContractConfig` still re-derives a stub's canonical type** with its own `startsWith` test instead of reading `entry.fullType`. It is the same class, and it agrees with `entry.fullType` for every stub this tree declares. It would diverge only for `registerLazy('ns:x', …, { namespace: 'ns' })`, which nothing declares. Left alone, as polish outside the claim's surface. Carrier: none.
4. **A live full-load pin** was added in patch round 1, after the seat widened the claim's surface to one console test file: `apps/console/src/__tests__/full-load-placeholder-race-11680.test.ts` (see Pins). The one-time measurement in the table above remains as the before/after reading on the real chunks.
5. `view:calendar` / `view:timeline` are not `DeclaredNode` types in `@object-ui/types`, so the pin declares them through `CustomNodeRegistry`. Observation only.
